_comment: Faction lore for the reference's Factions tab. Lore text and key art for RDL, UN and GoF are the publisher's, taken from the official faction pages. PD and COLLABORATION have no published lore and no key art, but they ARE factions at squad level - the app treats all five as real, so listing only three left a reader unable to find out what a PD card is or that it may join their squad. Their entries say what is known and are marked as ours rather than the publisher's. Both are currently `hidden`, which keeps them out of the Factions tab while OTTO decides how a non-lore faction should be presented - the text is kept here rather than deleted so it is ready when that is settled.

factions.name: Reconstruction Development League
factions.hook: Efficiency above all, directed by an algorithm.
factions.text:
The Reconstruction Development League is a faction that prioritizes efficiency. A super-coordination algorithm known as the "Guidance System" manages the schedules of all citizens to maximize overall well-being and drive rapid community development.

Most of this faction's combat equipment is produced by Tieling Heavy Industries. Their main battle units are cost-effective despite average performance, while elite units emphasize firepower and heavy armor. By strategically balancing these forces, you can overwhelm your opponents with a combination of pure firepower and numerical superiority.

factions.name: United Network
factions.hook: A corporate coalition of specialists and veteran PMCs.
factions.text:
The United Network is a highly commercialized corporate coalition that values skill specialization and leads in the research of ancient relic technology.

Its armed forces primarily consist of battle-hardened PMC units, offering a vast pool of elite pilots at your command. They are equipped with the most well-rounded and high-performance military gear, ensuring efficient mission execution.

Under the United Network, Red Dot Technologies and other suppliers provide advanced equipment for these forces. Their products excel in precision shooting and exceptional mobility, but come at a higher cost. As a result, you must carefully manage each soldier in your ranks.

factions.name: Guardians of Freedom
factions.hook: The smallest faction, fighting mostly with drones.
factions.text:
The Guardians of Freedom originated as a small community devoted to absolute free will.

As their influence grew, their commitment to preserving free will evolved into a deep reverence for the human mind. They reject consciousness digitization, making them the smallest of the three major factions. Even their mech pilots rely solely on brain-machine interfaces for control.

Their primary supplier, Wildfire Dynamics, is a rising tech company that emerged after the Great War. With the most advanced AI and drone technology in human civilization, the Guardians of Freedom rely heavily on unmanned units as the backbone of their forces, while a handful of powerful and costly mechs serve as the army's core.

factions.name: Planetring Dynamics
factions.hook: Mercenaries. They will fight for any of the three.
factions.text:
Planetring Dynamics is a mercenary supplier rather than one of the three powers, and the rulebook does not name it at all: everything below is drawn from how its cards are sold and played rather than from published lore.

What matters at the table is that PD units hire out. A PD mech may join an RDL, UN or GoF squad, which is what lets a small collection field a legal army. It is also the usual answer to the Guardians of Freedom having only one kit on sale.

Hiring them does not mix the parts. A PD mech is built entirely from PD parts and then joins your squad as a whole unit; you cannot bolt a PD arm onto an RDL mech, and its pilot has to be a PD pilot too. Its cards come from the LAB-CRISIS and Reaper kits and from the prerelease cores.

factions.name: White Dwarf Collaboration
factions.hook: A one-box crossover that fights as its own faction.
factions.text:
The White Dwarf is a crossover set rather than a faction with a story, and like Planetring Dynamics it appears nowhere in the rulebook. This entry is ours, not the publisher's.

It is a single box built around the ACE-001 White Dwarf, and it behaves as its own faction: its parts only combine with each other. Like PD it is mercenary, so the whole unit may join an RDL, UN or GoF squad.

One card to know about: its pilot Karl Fried is printed as Planetring Dynamics while shipping in the White Dwarf box. We treat him as part of this faction, because otherwise he could not legally pilot the mech he is sold with. The PD on his card most likely records who built the machine rather than who he fights for.
